claims.quote: It is lighted neither by window nor by lamp, yet it is filled with a soft radiance.
claims.description: Underground rooms are lit by sourceless artificial radiance with no windows or lamps.

claims.quote: There are no apertures for ventilation, yet the air is fresh.
claims.description: Sealed rooms have their air kept fresh by hidden mechanical air conditioning.

claims.quote: There are no musical instruments, and yet, at the moment that my meditation opens, this room is throbbing with melodious sounds.
claims.description: Music is piped on demand into every private room.

claims.quote: And in the arm-chair there sits a swaddled lump of flesh—a woman, about five feet high, with a face as white as a fungus.
claims.description: A machine-dependent life leaves humans physically shrunken, pale and weak.

claims.quote: The chair, like the music, was worked by machinery, and it rolled her to the other side of the room
claims.description: A motorized armchair carries its occupant around the room.

claims.quote: She knew several thousand people; in certain directions human intercourse had advanced enormously.
claims.description: Machine-mediated networks let one person keep in contact with thousands of acquaintances.

claims.quote: She touched the isolation knob, so that no one else could speak to her.
claims.description: An 'isolation' switch blocks all incoming calls, like a do-not-disturb mode.

claims.quote: A faint blue light shot across it, darkening to purple, and presently she could see the image of her son, who lived on the other side of the earth, and he could see her.
claims.description: A handheld plate gives two-way video calls between opposite sides of the earth.

claims.quote: It only gave a general idea of people—an idea that was good enough for all practical purposes, Vashti thought.
claims.description: Video communication strips out the nuances of expression, and society accepts the 'good enough' substitute for meeting face to face.

claims.quote: The air-ship barely takes two days to fly between me and you.
claims.description: Air-ships fly between the earth's hemispheres in under two days.

claims.quote: The surface of the earth is only dust and mud, no life remains on it, and you would need a respirator, or the cold of the outer air would kill you.
claims.description: The earth's surface is lifeless and its air deadly, so humanity lives underground and needs respirators outside.

claims.quote: Thrice she kissed it, thrice inclined her head, thrice she felt the delirium of acquiescence.
claims.description: People come to worship the Machine, performing private rituals over its Book.

claims.quote: There were buttons and switches everywhere—buttons to call for food, for music, for clothing.
claims.description: Push-button delivery of food, music and clothing to every room.

claims.quote: There was the hot-bath button, by pressure of which a basin of (imitation) marble rose out of the floor, filled to the brim with a warm deodorised liquid.
claims.description: A button raises a ready-filled bath out of the floor.

claims.quote: There was the button that produced literature.
claims.description: Literature is delivered on demand at the press of a button.

claims.quote: Vashti's next move was to turn off the isolation-switch, and all the accumulations of the last three minutes burst upon her.
claims.description: Messages queue while the user is unavailable and arrive all at once afterward, like notifications.

claims.quote: The clumsy system of public gatherings had been long since abandoned; neither Vashti nor her audience stirred from their rooms.
claims.description: Public gatherings are replaced by lectures given and attended remotely by video from private rooms.

claims.quote: She opened with a humorous account of music in the pre-Mongolian epoch, and went on to describe the great outburst of song that followed the Chinese conquest.
claims.description: A future history includes a Chinese conquest followed by a great outburst of song.

claims.quote: Complaint was useless, for beds were of the same dimension all over the world, and to have had an alternative size would have involved vast alterations in the Machine.
claims.description: All furnishings are standardized worldwide to suit the Machine.

claims.quote: Beneath those corridors of shining tiles were rooms, tier below tier, reaching far into the earth, and in each room there sat a human being, eating, or sleeping, or producing ideas.
claims.description: Humanity lives in deep underground cities of identical single-person cells.

claims.quote: Above her, beneath her, and around her, the Machine hummed eternally; she did not notice the noise, for she had been born with it in her ears.
claims.description: A single global Machine surrounds and supports all human life.

claims.quote: In it were instructions against every possible contingency.
claims.description: The Book of the Machine, published by the Central Committee, is a universal manual telling people which button to press for every need.

claims.quote: But she thought of Kuno as a baby, his birth, his removal to the public nurseries, her one visit to him there, his visits to her—visits which stopped when the Machine had assigned him a room on the other side of the earth.
claims.description: Children are removed to public nurseries at birth, and the Machine assigns each adult a room anywhere on earth.

claims.quote: cease at the moment of birth
claims.description: The Book of the Machine declares that parents' duties end at a child's birth.

claims.quote: She would summon a car and it would fly with her down the tunnel until it reached the lift that communicated with the air-ship station
claims.description: On-call tunnel cars carry passengers from their rooms to lifts and air-ship stations.

claims.quote: the civilisation that had mistaken the functions of the system, and had used it for bringing people to things, instead of for bringing things to people.
claims.description: Transport systems shift from moving people to delivering goods to stationary people.

claims.quote: Immediately an enormous apparatus fell on to her out of the ceiling, a thermometer was automatically inserted between her lips, a stethoscope was automatically laid upon her heart.
claims.description: Automated medical apparatus drops from the ceiling to examine a patient at home.

claims.quote: Vashti drank the medicine that the doctor projected into her mouth, and the machinery retired into the ceiling.
claims.description: Remote doctors treat patients at home through the Machine, delivering medicine directly.

claims.quote: Few travelled in these days, for, thanks to the advance of science, the earth was exactly alike all over.
claims.description: Technology makes every place on earth identical, so almost no one travels.

claims.quote: Vessel after vessel would rise from the vomitories of Rye or of Christchurch (I use the antique names), would sail into the crowded sky, and would draw up at the wharves of the south—empty.
claims.description: A vast air-ship fleet keeps running on schedule though most ships fly empty.

claims.quote: So nicely adjusted was the system, so independent of meteorology, that the sky, whether calm or cloudy, resembled a vast kaleidoscope whereon the same patterns periodically recurred.
claims.description: Global air traffic runs on precise schedules regardless of weather.

claims.quote: Night and day, wind and storm, tide and earthquake, impeded man no longer.
claims.description: Technology overcomes all natural obstacles of weather, tide and earthquake.

claims.quote: In the rooms, if the Book was dropped, the floor raised it mechanically
claims.description: Floors automatically lift dropped objects back up.

claims.quote: Of course a revolving platform ran the length of the boat
claims.description: Moving walkways run the length of air-ships.

claims.quote: People never touched one another.
claims.description: Physical touch between people becomes obsolete because of the Machine.

claims.quote: Racing aeroplanes had been built for the purpose, capable of enormous speed, and steered by the greatest intellects of the epoch.
claims.description: A past era builds very fast racing aeroplanes to circle the globe and keep pace with the sun.

claims.quote: Science could prolong the night, but only for a little, and those high hopes of neutralising the earth's diurnal revolution had passed, together with hopes that were possibly higher.
claims.description: Hopes of neutralizing the effect of the earth's rotation (outrunning the sun) are abandoned as unattainable.

claims.quote: the Committee of the Machine, at the time rising into prominence, declared the pursuit illegal, unmechanical, and punishable by Homelessness.
claims.description: A Committee of the Machine rises to power and bans activities it deems 'unmechanical'.

claims.quote: The victim is exposed to the air, which kills him.
claims.description: 'Homelessness', expulsion to the lethal surface, is used as capital punishment.

claims.quote: Dawn, midday, twilight, the zodiacal path, touched neither men's lives nor their hearts, and science retreated into the ground, to concentrate herself upon problems that she was certain of solving.
claims.description: Humanity loses all interest in the heavens, and science turns inward to safe, solvable problems.

claims.quote: The forests had been destroyed during the literature epoch for the purpose of making newspaper-pulp
claims.description: The world's forests are destroyed to make newspaper pulp.

claims.quote: In the plain were seen the ruins of cities, with diminished rivers creeping by their walls, and by the sides of these were sometimes the signs of vomitories, marking the cities of today.
claims.description: Surface cities lie in ruins beside shrunken rivers, with underground cities beneath them.

claims.quote: There were eight or ten of them, mostly young males, sent out from the public nurseries to inhabit the rooms of those who had died in various parts of the earth.
claims.description: Young people raised in public nurseries are dispatched worldwide to fill the rooms of the dead.

claims.quote: He had been sent to Sumatra for the purpose of propagating the race.
claims.description: The Machine dispatches selected people around the world to breed.

claims.quote: For Kuno had lately asked to be a father, and his request had been refused by the Committee.
claims.description: Parenthood requires Committee permission, granted only to types the Machine wants passed on.

claims.quote: Each infant was examined at birth, and all who promised undue strength were destroyed.
claims.description: Newborns are screened and those likely to be physically strong are killed: eugenic infanticide.

claims.quote: We say 'space is annihilated,' but we have annihilated not space, but the sense thereof.
claims.description: Instant communication and transport destroy people's sense of distance and space.

claims.quote: Had they been destroyed by all the food-tubes and medicine-tubes and music-tubes that the Machine has evolved lately?
claims.description: Pipes deliver food, medicine and music throughout the underground city.

claims.quote: one simply summons a respirator and gets an Egression-permit.
claims.description: Visits to the surface require an official Egression-permit and a respirator.

claims.quote: I don't think you irreligious, for there is no such thing as religion left.
claims.description: Religion and superstition are abolished by the Machine.

claims.quote: I climbed with my respirator and my hygienic clothes and my dietetic tabloids!
claims.description: People carry dietetic food tablets, hygienic clothing and respirators.
